concepts.why: The patient presented with acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain and was found to have a perforated appendix with a collection and surrounding fat stranding on CT scan.
The patient has a history of prostate cancer in remission and was found to have innumerable hepatic nodules and bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy on CT scan.
The patient presented with fever, tachycardia, and pulmonary consolidation on CT scan.
The patient was found to have a thickened, woody sigmoid colon on exploratory laparotomy and had a history of prostate cancer in remission.
The patient presented with fever, hypotension, and tachycardia, and had a perforated appendix with peritonism.
The patient has a history of emphysema.
The patient has a history of hypertension.
The patient underwent exploratory laparotomy and was found to have a thickened, woody sigmoid colon.
The patient required ventilation and had pulmonary consolidation on CT scan.
The patient had a combination of septic shock, respiratory failure, and metastatic cancer, leading to multi-organ failure.

rationales.F02: Heavy cigarette smoking increases the risk of various diseases, including lung cancer and cardiovascular disease.
rationales.F05: Prostate cancer in remission could indicate a history of cancer, which may be relevant to the current condition.
rationales.F06: Acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain is a common symptom of appendicitis.
rationales.F10: A perforated appendix with surrounding fat stranding is a strong indicator of appendicitis.
rationales.F11: Innumerable hepatic nodules could indicate metastatic disease, which may be related to the patient's history of prostate cancer.
rationales.F12: Bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy is a strong indicator of lymphoma or metastatic disease.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient presented with acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain, fever, hypotension, and tachycardia, which are all consistent with septic shock, and the perforated appendix is the likely source of the infection.
